marker_summary: pi-usereq 0.91.0: notification-only diff; fix MCP/workflow FPs

release_comparison.provenance: Original npm tarballs and .forage.json records retained in scratch/version-drift-b21699/prior; supplied release matches npm registry SHA-512 integrity.
release_comparison.decisive_diff: Manifest and README version bumps; runtime changes only fix ended-run duration, prompt association, completion notification gating, and coherent worktree completion state. The postinstall script, dependencies, notification transport, debug code, update scripts, and assets are unchanged.
release_comparison.queue_premise: The earlier no-detection premise does not reproduce: 0.89.0 and 0.90.0 also produce the same suspicious approval-map alert under the current rules.

execution_paths: package.json postinstall launches Node with tsx and scripts/install-static-checkers.ts. main gates approvePendingInstallScripts on npm_lifecycle_event=postinstall. Consumer root comes from npm_config_local_prefix, falling back to INIT_CWD.

The hook enumerates consumer node_modules including scoped packages, reads manifests, selects nonempty preinstall/install/postinstall scripts, adds missing unversioned allowScripts=true entries, preserves existing false entries, and writes consumer package.json. This broadly expands future script consent and merits the retained suspicious rule.

The remaining hook probes declared pyright/ruff/eslint executables and launches npm install with an argument vector only for missing checkers. Native checker installation commands are printed as guidance, not executed.
Pi registers project-analysis tools and prompt/worktree workflows. Tool subprocess execution, local file operations, and cleanup match that purpose.

agent_end triggers configured detached shell notification/sound commands. Pushover uses the official HTTPS messages endpoint with configured user/token credentials and templated result/output; global and per-event settings gate delivery. Defaults disable network notifications.

Debug request, session, and prompt files are local writes gated by DEBUG_ENABLED and DEBUG_PROMPTS_ENABLED. Replay curl text is generated as debugging metadata. Update scripts fetch documented upstream GitHub prompt/source repositories.
No obfuscated executable stage was found in the relevant paths. High-entropy MP3 notification assets and verbose source documentation are unchanged from the earlier release.

corrections.change: Preserve the original matcher and notable severity as metadata/lang/source/syntax/call::tool-method-call-syntax. The MCP refinement requires that observation plus same-file MCP constructor/transport or server SDK import evidence. Generic callable registration remains covered by micro-behaviors/data/llm/agent::tool-registration-call.

consumer_review.ancestor_selectors: Reviewed communications/mcp and build/ci/trigger ancestor selectors. The two Apex archive consumers now reference the unchanged neutral registration-syntax matcher alongside their independently required MCP constructor, preserving their original archive-wide observation sets. The SDK command-tool consumer uses the refined same-file MCP observation.
consumer_review.retained_coverage: All 12 ESM/CommonJS SDK runtime server examples retain MCP registration. Existing hostile/suspicious findings on the 407 externally checked analysis units are unchanged. Focused controls exercise all three exact MCP consumers, generic Pi registration, unrelated tool calls, and real workflow templates. A split-module archive control requires both Apex consumers even when registration is in a helper without its own MCP constructor.
consumer_review.external_losses: Only the SDK ESM/CommonJS mcp.d.ts units lose the MCP-registration claim: their old match was the comment Server.tool(), not a registration call. Both retain the unchanged textual observation in its neutral syntax home.
consumer_review.external_sample_availability: The mcp-conceal outside-batch archive was present for before/after checks, then disappeared from the shared samples directory before the final repeated run. Its completed comparisons are retained as positive-before.json and positive-after.json; final recheck uses the other five artifacts.

scan_comparison.material_detection_losses: Only the two unsupported workflow/MCP claims disappear from the archive and src/index.ts. The generic registration/syntax and every other pre-existing finding are retained. An existing Node file-read finding additionally surfaces in src/index.ts.
scan_comparison.disagreement: Calibrated ML classification remains benign (both route classes 0, level -1). The retained suspicious policy observation is accurate despite the overall BENIGN judgement. LPM blocking alone does not establish a compromised release.
scan_comparison.scan_caveats: Atomscan warns that its v18 model sees newer v19-only features as zero. Local scan results complete successfully; optional Hopper upload retries fail. The saved-report renderer rejects a dangling source ID, so comparison uses the raw JSON reports directly.

limitations: No deployment configuration was supplied and no package or dependency code was executed. The judgement concerns the supplied archive and inspected release difference; actual execution of user-configured notification commands was not observed.
final_required_check: make validate (run after writing this report and the judgement marker)
